Mission 1

8 ÷ 2(2 + 2): is the answer 1 or 16?

Make a guess: 8 ÷ 2(2 + 2): is the answer 1 or 16?

Number · place value and the order of operations

Place value and ordering numbers

  • Each column is worth 10 times the one to its right. ×10× 10, ×100× 100, ×1000× 1000 move digits 1, 2, 3 places left: 3.7×100=3703.7 × 100 = 370, 52÷1000=0.05252 ÷ 1000 = 0.052.
  • Compare decimals column by column from the left. On a number line, further right is bigger: −7<−2−7 < −2.
  • Symbols: ==, =≠ (not equal to), <<, >>, ≤≤ (less than or equal to), ≥≥ (greater than or equal to).
Quick check
?Which list is in order, smallest first? −0.6−0.6, −0.65−0.65, 0.060.06, 201​1/20
Number · place value and the order of operations

Negative numbers and reciprocals

  • Adding a negative is the same as subtracting: −6+(−2)=−8−6 + (−2) = −8. Subtracting a negative is the same as adding: 5−(−3)=85 − (−3) = 8.
  • Multiplying or dividing: same signs give a positive, different signs give a negative. (−4)×(−5)=20(−4) × (−5) = 20, −12÷3=−4−12 ÷ 3 = −4.
  • The reciprocal of a number is 1 divided by it: the reciprocal of 4 is 41​1/4, the reciprocal of 32​2/3 is 23​3/2.
  • A number times its reciprocal is 1. Zero has no reciprocal.
Calculate
?At 6 pm the temperature was 3 °C. It fell by 11 degrees by midnight, then rose by 5 degrees by 6 am. What was the temperature at 6 am?
°C
Number · place value and the order of operations

The order of operations

  • Order: Brackets, Indices (powers, roots), Division and Multiplication, Addition and Subtraction.
  • ×× and ÷÷ have equal priority: work them left to right. So do ++ and −−.
  • A number next to a bracket means multiply: 3(4+1)=3×53(4 + 1) = 3 × 5. A fraction line and a square root sign group like brackets.
  • Inverse operations undo each other (++ and −−, ×× and ÷÷, squaring and square-rooting). Check 223−98=125223 − 98 = 125 with 125+98=223125 + 98 = 223.
  • Calculator: bracket a fraction's top and bottom; round only the final answer.
Worked example Number · place value and the order of operations

Using the order of operations

Question
Work out 30−2×(1+3)2÷430 − 2 × (1 + 3)² ÷ 4
  1. 1
    Brackets first: 1+3=41 + 3 = 4, so the expression is 30−2×42÷430 − 2 × 4² ÷ 4
  2. 2
    Then the power: 42=164² = 16, giving 30−2×16÷430 − 2 × 16 ÷ 4
  3. 3
    Multiply and divide, left to right: 2×16=322 × 16 = 32, then 32÷4=832 ÷ 4 = 8
  4. 4
    Finally subtract: 30−8=2230 − 8 = 22
Answer
22
⚠️ Watch out
working left to right from the start (30−2=2830 − 2 = 28 first) gives 112. Subtraction waits until the end.
Calculate
?Work out −2(−4)2−3×23​((−4)² − 3 × 2³)/(−2) without a calculator.
Number · place value and the order of operations

Binary numbers

  • Our everyday numbers are base 10 (denary): column values 1, 10, 100, 1000, …
  • Binary is base 2: only the digits 0 and 1, with column values 1, 2, 4, 8, 16, 32, … (each double the last).
  • Binary to denary: add the column values where there is a 1. 11012​=8+4+1=131101₂ = 8 + 4 + 1 = 13.
  • Denary to binary: take out the biggest power of 2 that fits, then the next. 25=16+8+1=110012​25 = 16 + 8 + 1 = 11001₂.
Calculate
?Convert the binary number 1011012​101101₂ to denary (base 10).
Mission check

?8÷2(2+2)8 ÷ 2(2 + 2): using the order of operations, what is its value?

Following the order of operations you have learned, brackets give 8÷2×48 ÷ 2 × 4, and division and multiplication go left to right: 16. People who get 1 are treating 2(2+2)2(2+2) as a single block. Because the layout causes arguments, exam papers add brackets, such as (8÷2)(2+2)(8 ÷ 2)(2+2) or 2(2+2)8​8/(2(2+2)), so the meaning is never in doubt.

Mission 2

Two lights flash every 12 s and 18 s. When do they flash together?

Make a guess: Two lights flash every 12 s and 18 s. When do they flash together?

Number · factors, multiples and primes

Factors, multiples and primes

  • A factor (divisor) of a number divides into it exactly. Factors come in pairs: 36=1×36=2×18=3×12=4×9=6×636 = 1 × 36 = 2 × 18 = 3 × 12 = 4 × 9 = 6 × 6.
  • A multiple of a number is in its times table: the multiples of 12 are 12, 24, 36, 48, …
  • A prime number has exactly two factors, 1 and itself. 1 is not prime (it has only one factor), and 2 is the only even prime.
  • Common factors are shared factors; common multiples appear in both times tables.
Sort it
?Sort each number.

Tap a statement, then tap the group it belongs in. Then press Check.

Number · factors, multiples and primes

Prime factor decomposition

  • Every whole number above 1 can be written as a product of prime factors in exactly one way (the unique factorisation theorem).
  • Use a factor tree or repeated division by primes, and stop when every branch ends in a prime.
  • Write the answer in index form, smallest prime first: 360=2×2×2×3×3×5=23×32×5360 = 2 × 2 × 2 × 3 × 3 × 5 = 2³ × 3² × 5.
  • Check by multiplying back: 8×9×5=3608 × 9 × 5 = 360.
Quick check
?Which is 600 written as a product of its prime factors?
Number · factors, multiples and primes

HCF and LCM

  • The highest common factor (HCF) is the biggest number that divides into both. The lowest common multiple (LCM) is the smallest number both divide into.
  • Listing: write out factors (HCF) or multiples (LCM) of each number until they match.
  • Prime factor method: put the prime factors in a Venn diagram, with shared primes in the overlap. HCF = product of the overlap; LCM = product of everything in the diagram.
  • Higher: for CCEA, the prime factor method is Higher (Unit M3).
Worked example Number · factors, multiples and primes

HCF and LCM using prime factors

Question
Find the HCF and the LCM of 84 and 90.
  1. 1
    Write each as a product of primes: 84=22×3×784 = 2² × 3 × 7, 90=2×32×590 = 2 × 3² × 5
  2. 2
    Place the shared primes (one 2 and one 3) in the overlap; left of it goes 2 and 7, right of it goes 3 and 5
  3. 3
    HCF is the overlap: 2×3=62 × 3 = 6
  4. 4
    LCM is everything: 2×7×2×3×3×5=12602 × 7 × 2 × 3 × 3 × 5 = 1260
Answer
HCF = 6, LCM = 1260
⚠️ Watch out
multiplying the two numbers (84×90=756084 × 90 = 7560) gives a common multiple, but not the lowest.
Calculate
?A teacher has 84 pencils and 120 rubbers. She puts them into identical packs, using every pencil and every rubber, with nothing left over. What is the greatest number of packs she can make?
Calculate
?A=23×3×52A = 2³ × 3 × 5² and B=2×32×5B = 2 × 3² × 5. Find the lowest common multiple of AA and BB.
Mission check

?Two lights flash together, then every 12 s and every 18 s. When do they next flash together?

They flash together whenever the time is a multiple of both 12 and 18, so the next time is the lowest common multiple. Listing gives 12, 24, 36 and 18, 36; with primes, 12=22×312 = 2² × 3 and 18=2×3218 = 2 × 3², so the LCM is 22×32=362² × 3² = 36 seconds.

Half a cup of milk, then a third of a cup more: is that 52​2/5 of a cup?

Make a guess: Half a cup of milk, then a third of a cup more: is that 52​2/5 of a cup?

Number · fractions

Equivalent fractions and mixed numbers

  • Equivalent fractions have the same value: multiply or divide the top and bottom by the same number. 32​=128​2/3 = 8/12.
  • Simplest form: divide top and bottom by their HCF. 2418​=43​18/24 = 3/4 (divide by 6).
  • A mixed number has a whole part and a fraction part. Improper to mixed: 411​=243​11/4 = 23/4 (4 goes into 11 twice, remainder 3).
  • Mixed to improper: whole × denominator, plus numerator, over the same denominator.
Quick check
?Write 352​32/5 as an improper fraction.
Number · fractions

Fractions of amounts

  • To find a fraction of an amount, divide by the denominator, multiply by the numerator: 52​2/5 of 35 is 35÷5×2=1435 ÷ 5 × 2 = 14.
  • "Of" means multiply: 52​2/5 of 35 is 52​×352/5 × 35.
  • To write one quantity as a fraction of another, put the first over the second (same units), then simplify: 45 minutes out of an hour is 6045​=43​45/60 = 3/4.
  • A fraction can be greater than 1: 90 minutes as a fraction of an hour is 6090​=23​90/60 = 3/2.
Calculate
?A school has 840 students. 73​3/7 of them walk to school. 41​1/4 of the rest come by bus. How many students come by bus?
Number · fractions

Adding and subtracting fractions

  • You can only add or subtract fractions when the pieces are the same size: rewrite them with a common denominator (the LCM of the denominators is the neatest).
  • Then add or subtract the numerators; the denominator stays the same. 41​+61​=123​+122​=125​1/4 + 1/6 = 3/12 + 2/12 = 5/12.
  • Never add the denominators.
  • With mixed numbers, the safest route is to change to improper fractions first. Negative fractions follow the usual sign rules: −21​+31​=−63​+62​=−61​−1/2 + 1/3 = −3/6 + 2/6 = −1/6.
Worked example Number · fractions

Subtracting mixed numbers

Question
Work out 243​−165​23/4 − 15/6
  1. 1
    Change to improper fractions: 411​−611​11/4 − 11/6
  2. 2
    Use the common denominator 12: 1233​−1222​33/12 − 22/12
  3. 3
    Subtract the numerators: 1211​11/12
Answer
1211​11/12
⚠️ Watch out
splitting into 2−1=12 − 1 = 1 and then working out 65​−43​5/6 − 3/4 (because 43​−65​3/4 − 5/6 looks impossible) gives 1121​11/12, which is wrong.
Quick check
?Work out 32​+43​2/3 + 3/4
Number · fractions

Multiplying and dividing fractions

  • To multiply, multiply the numerators and multiply the denominators, cancelling first if you can: 32​×109​=3018​=53​2/3 × 9/10 = 18/30 = 3/5.
  • Dividing by a number is the same as multiplying by its reciprocal: 3÷5=3×51​=53​3 ÷ 5 = 3 × 1/5 = 3/5.
  • So to divide by a fraction, flip the second fraction and multiply: 43​÷52​=43​×25​=815​3/4 ÷ 2/5 = 3/4 × 5/2 = 15/8.
  • Change mixed numbers to improper fractions first. Signs as usual: −21​×32​=−31​−1/2 × 2/3 = −1/3.
Calculate
?A plank is 343​33/4 m long. It is cut into pieces that are each 85​5/8 m long. How many pieces are there? Do not use a calculator.
Mission check

?Half a cup of milk, then a third of a cup more. How much milk is that?

The note is wrong: 52​2/5 is less than 21​1/2, yet milk was added. Halves and thirds are different-sized pieces, so change both to sixths: 63​+62​=65​3/6 + 2/6 = 5/6 of a cup.

Is 0.999… (nines forever) exactly equal to 1?

Number · fractions, decimals and percentages

Converting between fractions, decimals and percentages

  • Percent means "number of parts per hundred": 60%=10060​=0.660% = 60/100 = 0.6.
  • Fraction to decimal: divide the numerator by the denominator. 53​=3÷5=0.63/5 = 3 ÷ 5 = 0.6.
  • Decimal to fraction: use place value, then simplify. 0.35=10035​=207​0.35 = 35/100 = 7/20.
  • Decimal to percentage: multiply by 100. 47​=1.75=175%7/4 = 1.75 = 175%.
  • To order a mix of forms, change them all to decimals first.
Worked example Number · fractions, decimals and percentages

Converting both ways

Question
Write 0.45 as a fraction in its simplest form, and write 83​3/8 as a percentage.
  1. 1
    0.45 is 45 hundredths: 10045​45/100
  2. 2
    Divide top and bottom by 5: 209​9/20
  3. 3
    Divide 3 by 8 (short division, 3.000÷83.000 ÷ 8): 0.3750.375
  4. 4
    Multiply by 100: 37.5%37.5%
Answer
0.45=209​0.45 = 9/20 and 83​=37.5%3/8 = 37.5%
⚠️ Watch out
83​3/8 is not 3.8% or 38%. Divide the numerator by the denominator; don't just write the digits next to each other.
Calculate
?400 people were asked how they travel to work. 83​3/8 cycle, 0.3 walk, 22% take the bus and the rest drive. How many drive?
Number · fractions, decimals and percentages

Terminating and recurring decimals

  • A terminating decimal stops: 403​=0.0753/40 = 0.075. A recurring decimal repeats for ever: 31​=0.333…1/3 = 0.333…, 61​=0.1666…1/6 = 0.1666…, 115​=0.4545…5/11 = 0.4545…
  • A fraction in its simplest form terminates exactly when its denominator has no prime factors other than 2 and 5 (because 10=2×510 = 2 × 5). Otherwise it recurs.
  • Every recurring decimal is an exact fraction, even though its digits never end.
  • Higher: Rational: can be written as ba​a/b, aa and bb integers (b=0b ≠ 0). Irrational (2​√2, ππ): the decimal never ends or repeats.
Sort it
?Does each fraction give a terminating or a recurring decimal? Simplify first.

Tap a statement, then tap the group it belongs in. Then press Check.

Number · fractions, decimals and percentages

Recurring decimals to fractions (Higher)

  • Dot notation: a dot over a digit shows it repeats. 0.4˙=0.444…0.4 = 0.444…, 0.17˙=0.1777…0.17 = 0.1777…, 0.1˙2˙=0.121212…0.12 = 0.121212…, 0.1˙23˙=0.123123…0.123 = 0.123123… (dots on the first and last digit of the repeating block).
  • Method: call the decimal xx. Multiply by 10, 100, … so the repeating parts line up, then subtract to remove them.
  • One repeating digit: multiply by 10. Two: multiply by 100. Then solve for xx and simplify.
  • Fraction to recurring decimal: divide, as on screen 4.
Worked example Number · fractions, decimals and percentages

Converting 0.27˙0.27 to a fraction (Higher)

Question
Write 0.27˙0.27 as a fraction in its simplest form.
  1. 1
    Let x=0.2777…x = 0.2777…
  2. 2
    Multiply by 10 and by 100: 10x=2.777…10x = 2.777… and 100x=27.777…100x = 27.777… (the recurring parts now line up)
  3. 3
    Subtract: 100x−10x=27.777…−2.777…100x − 10x = 27.777… − 2.777…, so 90x=2590x = 25
  4. 4
    Solve and simplify: x=9025​=185​x = 25/90 = 5/18
Answer
185​5/18
⚠️ Watch out
subtracting xx from 10x10x here doesn't work, because 2.777…−0.2777…2.777… − 0.2777… doesn't cancel the recurring part. Line up the repeating digits first.
Calculate
?(Higher) Write 0.4˙5˙0.45 as a fraction in its simplest form. Enter the denominator of your fraction.

Mission check

?Is 0.999… (nines for ever) exactly equal to 1?

They are exactly equal. Since 31​=0.333…1/3 = 0.333…, multiplying by 3 gives 1=0.999…1 = 0.999… Higher check: let x=0.9˙x = 0.9; then 10x−x=9.999…−0.999…=910x − x = 9.999… − 0.999… = 9, so 9x=99x = 9 and x=1x = 1.

Mission 5

Fold a sheet of paper 42 times. Would it reach the Moon?

Make a guess: Fold a sheet of paper 42 times. Would it reach the Moon?

Number · powers and indices

Powers, roots and repeated doubling

  • 53=5×5×5=1255³ = 5 × 5 × 5 = 125: the base is 5 and the index (power) is 3.
  • Learn the squares to 152=22515² = 225, the cubes of 1 to 5 and 10, and 25=322⁵ = 32, 34=813⁴ = 81, 10610⁶ (a million).
  • A root undoes a power: 169​=13√169 = 13, 364​=4∛64 = 4. A positive number has two square roots, e.g. ±13± 13.
  • Each fold doubles the thickness, so nn folds multiply it by 2n2ⁿ.
Number · powers and indices

The three laws of indices

  • Multiplying powers of the same base: add the indices. am×an=am+na^m × aⁿ = a^(m+n)
  • Dividing: subtract the indices. am÷an=am−na^m ÷ aⁿ = a^(m−n)
  • A power of a power: multiply the indices. (am)n=amn(a^m)ⁿ = a^mn
  • The laws only work when the bases are the same: 23×522³ × 5² cannot be combined.
  • Shortcut: 210=1024≈10002¹⁰ = 1024 ≈ 1000, so 240=(210)4≈10122⁴⁰ = (2¹⁰)⁴ ≈ 10¹².
Worked example Number · powers and indices

Using the laws on an algebraic expression

Question
Simplify (2x3)2×3x4÷6x5(2x³)² × 3x⁴ ÷ 6x⁵.
  1. 1
    Square everything in the bracket, numbers too: (2x3)2=4x6(2x³)² = 4x⁶
  2. 2
    Multiply numbers, add indices: 4x6×3x4=12x104x⁶ × 3x⁴ = 12x¹⁰
  3. 3
    Divide numbers, subtract indices: 12x10÷6x5=2x512x¹⁰ ÷ 6x⁵ = 2x⁵
Answer
2x52x⁵
⚠️ Watch out
writing (2x3)2=2x6(2x³)² = 2x⁶ forgets to square the 2, and leads to x5x⁵.
Calculate
?A sheet of paper is 0.1 mm thick. Each fold doubles the thickness. What is the smallest number of folds that makes it thicker than 1 metre?
Number · powers and indices

Zero and negative indices

  • 23÷23=202³ ÷ 2³ = 2⁰, but any number divided by itself is 1. So a0=1a⁰ = 1 (for a=0a ≠ 0).
  • A negative index means a reciprocal: a−n=an1​a⁻ⁿ = 1/aⁿ
  • 2−3=231​=81​2⁻³ = 1/2³ = 1/8 and 52÷54=5−2=251​5² ÷ 5⁴ = 5⁻² = 1/25
  • A negative index never makes the answer negative.
  • Higher: on CCEA, zero and negative indices are Higher tier (Unit M7).
Quick check
?What is the value of 4−24⁻²?
Number · powers and indices

Fractional indices (Higher)

  • The denominator of a fractional index is a root: an1​=na​a^(1/n) = n√a, so 1621​=416^(1/2) = 4 and 8141​=381^(1/4) = 3.
  • The numerator is a power: anm​=(na​)ma^(m/n) = (n√a)^m. Take the root first to keep numbers small: 832​=22=48^(2/3) = 2² = 4.
  • A negative fractional index: reciprocal, then root, then power. 32−51​=21​32^(−1/5) = 1/2
  • For a fraction, flip it to deal with the minus sign: (ba​)−n=(ab​)n(a/b)⁻ⁿ = (b/a)ⁿ
Calculate
?Work out (1258​)−32​(8/125)^(−2/3). Give your answer as a decimal. (Higher)
Mission check

?Fold a 0.1 mm sheet of paper 42 times. Would it reach the Moon, about 384,400 km away?

Yes, in theory. Each fold doubles the thickness, so 42 folds multiply 0.1 mm by 242≈4.4×10122⁴² ≈ 4.4 × 10¹². That is about 440,000 km, further than the Moon. Repeated doubling grows astonishingly fast; that is what an index shows.

Mission 6

Are you a billion seconds old yet?

Make a guess: Are you a billion seconds old yet?

Number · standard form

Writing a number in standard form

  • Standard form is A×10nA × 10ⁿ, where 1≤A<101 ≤ A < 10 and nn is an integer.
  • Big numbers have a positive power: 3450000=3.45×1063 450 000 = 3.45 × 10⁶ (the point moves 6 places).
  • Small numbers have a negative power: 0.00072=7.2×10−40.000 72 = 7.2 × 10⁻⁴.
  • One billion is 1×1091 × 10⁹. A calculator may show 3.2×10−53.2 × 10⁻⁵ as 3.2E-05.
  • Higher: on CCEA this is called standard index form and is Higher tier (Unit M7).
Worked example Number · standard form

Converting in both directions

Question
(a) Write 0.000 305 in standard form. (b) Write 4.06×1054.06 × 10⁵ as an ordinary number.
  1. 1
    (a) Place the point after the first non-zero digit: A=3.05A = 3.05
  2. 2
    (a) The point moves 4 places right, so the power is −4−4: 3.05×10−43.05 × 10⁻⁴
  3. 3
    (b) Multiplying by 10510⁵ moves the point 5 places right: 406000406 000
Answer
(a) 3.05×10−43.05 × 10⁻⁴ (b) 406,000
⚠️ Watch out
counting zeros instead of places moved. 0.000 305 has five zeros in total, but the point moves only 4 places.
Sort it

Number · standard form

Ordering and calculating

  • To order, compare the powers first, then AA: 6.1×10−3<2.4×10−26.1 × 10⁻³ < 2.4 × 10⁻².
  • Multiply: multiply the AA values and add the powers.
  • Divide: divide the AA values and subtract the powers.
  • Add or subtract: first rewrite both numbers with the same power of 10 (or as ordinary numbers).
  • Finally adjust so that 1≤A<101 ≤ A < 10.
Worked example Number · standard form

Multiplying without a calculator

Question
Work out (6×104)×(5×10−7)(6 × 10⁴) × (5 × 10⁻⁷). Give your answer in standard form.
  1. 1
    Multiply the numbers: 6×5=306 × 5 = 30
  2. 2
    Add the powers: 104×10−7=10−310⁴ × 10⁻⁷ = 10⁻³
  3. 3
    Combine: 30×10−330 × 10⁻³, which is not yet standard form
  4. 4
    Adjust: 30=3×10130 = 3 × 10¹, so 3×101×10−3=3×10−23 × 10¹ × 10⁻³ = 3 × 10⁻²
Answer
3×10−23 × 10⁻²
⚠️ Watch out
stopping at 30×10−330 × 10⁻³ loses the final mark because AA is not less than 10.

Mission check

?Are you a billion seconds old yet? (A year is about 3.16×1073.16 × 10⁷ seconds.)

Not yet. A year has 365.25×24×60×60≈3.16×107365.25 × 24 × 60 × 60 ≈ 3.16 × 10⁷ seconds, and a billion seconds divided by this is about 31.7 years. You reach a billion seconds at about 31 years 8 months. A quick estimate, 109÷(3×107)≈3310⁹ ÷ (3 × 10⁷) ≈ 33, gets you close without a calculator.

Number · accuracy and bounds

Decimal places and significant figures

  • Decimal places (d.p.) count digits after the decimal point: 3.14159 to 2 d.p. is 3.14.
  • Significant figures (s.f.) count from the first non-zero digit: 0.047 38 to 2 s.f. is 0.047.
  • Look at the next digit: 5 or more rounds up. Keep place-value zeros: 52,861 to 2 s.f. is 53,000.
  • Never round in the middle of a calculation: keep full calculator values and round only the final answer.
Quick check
?Round 0.030 96 to 2 significant figures.
Number · accuracy and bounds

Estimating by rounding

  • To estimate, round every number to 1 significant figure, then work it out by hand.
  • Use ≈≈ to show the answer is approximate: 0.193612×4.87​≈0.2600×5​=15000(612 × 4.87)/0.193 ≈ (600 × 5)/0.2 = 15 000
  • Dividing by a decimal such as 0.2 makes the answer bigger: 3000÷0.2=150003000 ÷ 0.2 = 15 000.
  • An estimate checks a calculator answer: the exact value here is about 15,400, so a result of 1540 would be wrong.
Calculate
?A school orders 289 books at £5.85 each. Estimate the total cost by rounding each number to 1 significant figure.
£
Number · accuracy and bounds

The bounds of a rounded measurement

  • 80 kg to the nearest 10 kg means anything from 75 kg up to, but not including, 85 kg.
  • Go half a unit either way: lower bound 75 kg, upper bound 85 kg.
  • As an inequality: 75≤m<8575 ≤ m < 85. 85 is excluded because it rounds up to 90.
  • Higher: on CCEA, upper and lower bounds are Higher tier (Units M3 and M4).
Quick check
?A length ll is 6.4 cm, correct to 1 decimal place. Which shows the possible values of ll?
Number · accuracy and bounds

Bounds in calculations (Higher)

  • To find the biggest or smallest possible result, choose the right bound for each value.
  • Add: upper + upper gives the upper bound. Multiply: upper × upper.
  • Subtract: upper − lower gives the upper bound (take away as little as possible).
  • Divide: upper ÷ lower gives the upper bound (divide by as little as possible).
  • For lower bounds, swap every choice. Then round only at the end, to a sensible accuracy.
Worked example Number · accuracy and bounds

The slowest possible speed (Higher)

Question
A runner covers 100 m, to the nearest metre, in 12.3 s, to 1 d.p. Find the lower bound of the speed, to 3 significant figures.
  1. 1
    Bounds of the distance: 99.5≤d<100.599.5 ≤ d < 100.5
  2. 2
    Bounds of the time: 12.25≤t<12.3512.25 ≤ t < 12.35
  3. 3
    Smallest speed = smallest distance ÷ largest time: 12.3599.5​=8.0566…99.5/12.35 = 8.0566…
  4. 4
    Round at the end: 8.06 m/s
Answer
8.06 m/s
⚠️ Watch out
using both lower bounds, 99.5÷12.2599.5 ÷ 12.25, gives 8.12 m/s, which is not the smallest speed.
Calculate
?A floor tile measures 30 cm by 20 cm, each correct to the nearest centimetre. Work out the upper bound of its area. Give your answer exactly. (Higher)
cm²
Mission check

?A lift can take 640 kg. Eight people step in, each 80 kg to the nearest 10 kg. Could the lift be overloaded?

Yes, it could be. "80 kg to the nearest 10 kg" means 75≤m<8575 ≤ m < 85 for each person, so eight people of 82 kg each are all labelled 80 kg yet weigh 656 kg, over the limit. The true total could be anything from 600 kg up to almost 680 kg, so the rounded labels can't promise the lift is safe.

Mission 8

Halve an A4 sheet and it keeps its shape. Why must that be 2​√2?

Make a guess: Halve an A4 sheet and it keeps its shape. Why must that be 2​√2?

Number · surds

What a surd is (Higher)

  • A surd is a root that cannot be simplified to a whole number or fraction, such as 2​√2 or 7​√7. It is irrational, so leaving it as 2​√2 keeps an answer exact.
  • 9​=3√9 = 3 is not a surd.
  • Multiply and divide inside one root: a​×b​=ab​√a × √b = √ab and b​a​​=ba​​(√a)/(√b) = √(a/b)
  • So a​×a​=a√a × √a = a: 2​×2​=2√2 × √2 = 2.
  • You cannot add inside a root: 9​+16​=7√9 + √16 = 7, but 25​=5√25 = 5.
Number · surds

Simplifying surds (Higher)

  • Split off the largest square factor: 12​=4×3​=4​×3​=23​√12 = √(4 × 3) = √4 × √3 = 2√3
  • Useful squares to look for: 4, 9, 16, 25, 36, 49, 64, 100.
  • Simplify first, then collect like surds as you would like terms:
200​−32​=102​−42​=62​√200 − √32 = 10√2 − 4√2 = 6√2
  • Different surds such as 2​√2 and 3​√3 cannot be combined by adding.
Quick check
?Simplify 75​+12​√75 + √12.
Worked example Number · surds

Expanding a bracket with a surd (Higher)

Question
Expand and simplify (4−3​)2(4 − √3)².
  1. 1
    Write it as two brackets: (4−3​)(4−3​)(4 − √3)(4 − √3)
  2. 2
    Multiply every term: 16−43​−43​+3​3​16 − 4√3 − 4√3 + √3√3
  3. 3
    Use 3​3​=3√3√3 = 3: 16−83​+316 − 8√3 + 3
  4. 4
    Collect the whole numbers: 19−83​19 − 8√3
Answer
19−83​19 − 8√3
⚠️ Watch out
(4−3​)2(4 − √3)² is not 16−316 − 3; squaring a bracket always gives a middle term.
Calculate
?Expand and simplify (5+2​)(5−2​)(5 + √2)(5 − √2). (Higher)
Number · surds

Rationalising the denominator (Higher)

  • Rationalise means rewrite a fraction so there is no surd in the denominator.
  • Multiply top and bottom by the surd: 5​10​=5105​​=25​10/(√5) = (10√5)/5 = 2√5
  • With a number in front, still multiply by the surd only: 32​5​=652​​5/(3√2) = (5√2)/6
  • In the same way, 2​2​=222​​=2​2/(√2) = (2√2)/2 = √2.
Calculate
?A rectangle has area 18 cm² and width 3​√3 cm. Its length is a3​a√3 cm. Find aa. (Higher)
Mission check

?An A-size sheet has sides in the ratio r:1r : 1. Half a sheet is the same shape. Why must r=2​r = √2?

Halving a sheet with sides rr and 1 gives a sheet with sides 1 and 2r​r/2, so its ratio is r2​2/r. Keeping the shape needs r=r2​r = 2/r, so r2=2r² = 2 and r=2​r = √2. Check: 2​2​=2​2/(√2) = √2, exactly the same ratio again.

Mission 9

A 4-digit PIN: how many guesses to be certain of getting it?

Make a guess: A 4-digit PIN: how many guesses to be certain of getting it?

Number · counting strategies

Listing systematically

  • Systematic listing means following a fixed order so that nothing is missed and nothing is repeated.
  • Fix the first choice, run through every option for the second, then move the first choice on.
  • A table or grid works well for two choices: rows for one, columns for the other.
  • Look for a structure you can count without writing everything out: the 2-digit codes 00, 01, …, 99 go from 0 to 99, so there are 100 of them.
Worked example Number · counting strategies

Listing arrangements

Question
Cards show the digits 1, 4 and 7. Each card is used once to make a 3-digit number. List all the numbers. How many are greater than 500?
  1. 1
    First digit 1, then the other two both ways: 147, 174
  2. 2
    First digit 4: 417, 471
  3. 3
    First digit 7: 714, 741
  4. 4
    That is 6 numbers. Those above 500 start with 7: 714 and 741
Answer
6 numbers; 2 are greater than 500
⚠️ Watch out
listing at random (147, 741, 417, …) is how numbers get missed or written twice. Fix the first digit each time.
Calculate
?A bag holds four counters numbered 1, 1, 2 and 5. Two counters are taken out and their numbers are added. How many different totals are possible?
Number · counting strategies

The product rule for counting (Higher)

  • If there are mm ways to do one thing and, for each of those, nn ways to do another, there are m×nm × n ways to do both.
  • It extends to more stages: multiply the number of choices at each stage. 3 starters, 4 mains and 2 desserts give 3×4×2=243 × 4 × 2 = 24 meals.
  • If an item can't be repeated, each stage has one fewer choice than the one before.
  • Deal with any restricted position first (for example, "the first digit can't be 0").
Worked example Number · counting strategies

Counting codes (Higher)

Question
A code is 2 letters (A to Z) followed by 3 digits (0 to 9). Letters and digits may repeat. How many different codes are there?
  1. 1
    Choices for each letter: 26, and for each digit: 10
  2. 2
    Multiply the choices: 26×26×10×10×1026 × 26 × 10 × 10 × 10
  3. 3
    Work it out: 676×1000=676000676 × 1000 = 676 000
Answer
676,000 codes
⚠️ Watch out
adding the choices (26+26+10+10+10=8226 + 26 + 10 + 10 + 10 = 82) counts single options, not whole codes. Each stage multiplies.
Quick check
?(Higher) How many 3-digit numbers (100 to 999) have no repeated digits?
Calculate
?(Higher) In a league of 15 teams, every team plays every other team exactly once. How many matches are played?
Mission check

?A 4-digit PIN uses the digits 0–9, and digits can repeat. How many guesses make you certain to get it?

Listed in order, the PINs run 0000, 0001, …, 9999, which is 10,000 codes (just as the 2-digit codes 00 to 99 make 100). With the product rule: 10 choices for each of 4 positions, 104=1000010⁴ = 10 000. To be certain you would need 10,000 guesses in the worst case; if no digit could repeat it would drop to 10×9×8×7=504010 × 9 × 8 × 7 = 5040.

Mission 10

Paint mixed 3 blue : 2 yellow. 8 L of blue makes how much paint?

Make a guess: Paint mixed 3 blue : 2 yellow. 8 L of blue makes how much paint?

Ratio · simplifying and sharing

Ratio notation and simplest form

  • A ratio a:ba : b compares the sizes of parts: 3 blue : 2 yellow means every 3 tins of blue go with 2 tins of yellow.
  • Simplify by dividing every part by the same number (the HCF): 12:18=2:312 : 18 = 2 : 3. Three-part ratios work the same way.
  • Write both quantities in the same units first, then drop the units.
  • The form 1:n1 : n: divide both parts by the first part. nn may be a decimal.
Worked example Ratio · simplifying and sharing

Simplest form and the form 1 : n

Question
Write 5050 cm :1.5: 1.5 m in its simplest form. Then write 12:3012 : 30 in the form 1:n1 : n.
  1. 1
    Change to the same units: 1.51.5 m =150= 150 cm, so the ratio is 50:15050 : 150
  2. 2
    Divide both parts by the HCF, 50: 50:150=1:350 : 150 = 1 : 3
  3. 3
    For 12:3012 : 30, divide both parts by 12: 1:1230​1 : 30/12
  4. 4
    Work out nn: 1230​=2.530/12 = 2.5
Answer
1:31 : 3 and 1:2.51 : 2.5
⚠️ Watch out
simplifying 50:1.550 : 1.5 without converting units gives a ratio that means nothing.
Quick check
?Write 45:60:7545 : 60 : 75 in its simplest form.
Ratio · simplifying and sharing

Sharing in a ratio

  • To share an amount in the ratio a:ba : b, add the parts to get the total number of parts.
  • One part = amount ÷ total parts. Multiply to get each share. Check the shares add back to the amount.
  • If you know one share instead (part : part), divide it by its own number of parts to find one part.
  • If you know the difference between two shares, divide it by the difference in their parts.
Worked example Ratio · simplifying and sharing

Sharing in a three-part ratio

Question
Share £416 in the ratio 4:3:14 : 3 : 1.
  1. 1
    Add the parts: 4+3+1=84 + 3 + 1 = 8 parts
  2. 2
    Find one part: 416÷8=52416 ÷ 8 = 52, so one part is £52
  3. 3
    Multiply each part: 4×52=2084 × 52 = 208, 3×52=1563 × 52 = 156, 1×52=521 × 52 = 52
  4. 4
    Check the total: 208+156+52=416208 + 156 + 52 = 416
Answer
£208, £156 and £52
⚠️ Watch out
dividing £416 by 4, 3 and 1 in turn (instead of by the 8 parts) gives shares that add to far more than £416.
Calculate
?In a school choir, the ratio of boys to girls is 3:53 : 5. There are 24 more girls than boys. How many students are in the choir altogether?
Ratio · simplifying and sharing

Ratios, fractions and combining ratios

  • 3:23 : 2 makes 5 parts: blue is 53​3/5 of the paint and yellow is 52​2/5.
  • Yellow is 32​2/3 of blue.
  • Mixes in this ratio lie on y=32​xy = 2/3x (blue xx, yellow yy): a straight line through the origin.
  • To combine a:ba : b and b:cb : c, make the bb parts equal: 2:32 : 3 and 4:54 : 5 become 8:128 : 12 and 12:1512 : 15, so 8:12:158 : 12 : 15.
Quick check
?In a box of pens, red : blue =3:4= 3 : 4 and blue : green =6:5= 6 : 5. Find red : green in its simplest form.
Calculate
?A concrete mix uses cement, sand and gravel in the ratio 1:2:41 : 2 : 4 by mass. A builder has 15 kg of sand and plenty of cement and gravel. What is the greatest mass of concrete mix she can make, using all the sand?
kg
Mission check

?Paint is mixed 3 blue : 2 yellow. You have 8 L of blue and plenty of yellow. How much paint can you make?

The 8 litres of blue are 3 equal parts, so one part is 38​8/3 litres. The paint has 5 parts, so you can make 340​40/3 litres, about 13.3 litres, using 531​51/3 litres of yellow.

Mission 11

A price goes up 20%, then down 20%. Is it back where it started?

Make a guess: A price goes up 20%, then down 20%. Is it back where it started?

Ratio and proportion · percentages

Percentages as multipliers

  • Per cent means "parts per hundred": 35%=10035​=0.3535% = 35/100 = 0.35. Percentages can exceed 100%: 150%=1.5150% = 1.5.
  • To find 35% of an amount, multiply by 0.35.
  • To increase by 15%, multiply by 1+0.15=1.151 + 0.15 = 1.15. To decrease by 15%, multiply by 1−0.15=0.851 − 0.15 = 0.85.
  • Two changes in a row: multiply by each multiplier in turn. Each change is a percentage of the amount at that moment.
Worked example Ratio and proportion · percentages

Increasing with a multiplier

Question
A bike costs £240. Its price increases by 15%. Find the new price.
  1. 1
    Write the multiplier: 100%+15%=115%100% + 15% = 115%, so multiply by 1.15
  2. 2
    Multiply: 240×1.15=276240 × 1.15 = 276
  3. 3
    Check with the "find and add" method: 15%15% of 240 is 3636, and 240+36=276240 + 36 = 276
Answer
£276
⚠️ Watch out
multiplying by 0.15 gives only the increase (£36), not the new price.
Quick check
?Which single multiplier decreases an amount by 7%?
Ratio and proportion · percentages

Percentage change and one quantity as a percentage of another

  • To write AA as a percentage of BB: BA​×100A/B × 100. For example, 18 out of 24 is 2418​×100=75%18/24 × 100 = 75%.
  • Percentage change =originalchange​×100= change/original × 100. Always divide by the original value.
  • Percentage profit or loss uses the cost price as the original. To compare two scores out of different totals, turn both into percentages.
  • Simple interest: the same interest is paid each year, worked out on the original amount only.
Calculate
?A trader buys a bike for £350 and sells it for £294. Find her percentage loss.
Ratio and proportion · percentages

Reverse percentages (Higher)

  • In a reverse percentage (original value) problem you know the amount after the change.
  • Write the multiplier for the change, then divide by it: original == new amount ÷÷ multiplier.
  • After a 30% reduction, the price is 70% of the original, so divide by 0.7.
  • Check by applying the change to your answer.
Worked example Ratio and proportion · percentages

Finding the original price (Higher)

Question
In a sale, prices are reduced by 30%. A coat costs £42 in the sale. Find its price before the sale.
  1. 1
    Write the multiplier for the change: 100%−30%=70%100% − 30% = 70%, so ×0.7× 0.7
  2. 2
    Set up: original ×0.7=42× 0.7 = 42
  3. 3
    Divide by the multiplier: 42÷0.7=6042 ÷ 0.7 = 60
  4. 4
    Check: 30%30% of 60 is 1818, and 60−18=4260 − 18 = 42
Answer
£60
⚠️ Watch out
adding 30% to £42 gives £54.60. The 30% was taken off the original price, not the sale price.
Calculate
?After a 20% tax is added, the price of a printer is £186. Find the price before the tax was added. (Higher)
£
Calculate
?Rana invests £2,400 at 3.5% per year simple interest. What is the smallest whole number of years after which her total interest is at least £500?
Mission check

?A price goes up by 20%, then down by 20%. Is it back where it started?

No. The 20% increase multiplies the price by 1.2 and the 20% decrease multiplies by 0.8. Together that is ×0.96× 0.96, so a £100 jacket goes to £120 and then down to £96: 4% lower than it started.

Mission 12

Money grows at 5% a year compound interest. When has it doubled?

Make a guess: Money grows at 5% a year compound interest. When has it doubled?

Ratio and proportion · growth and decay

Compound interest

  • Simple interest is the same every year: it is always worked out on the original amount.
  • Compound interest is added to the balance, so next year's interest is worked out on a bigger amount: interest earns interest.
  • Each year at 5%, multiply by 1.05. After nn years: amount == original ×1.05n× 1.05ⁿ.
  • The interest earned is the final amount minus the original amount.
Worked example Ratio and proportion · growth and decay

Compound interest over three years

Question
£1,000 is invested at 5% per year compound interest. Find the amount after 3 years, and the interest earned.
  1. 1
    Write the multiplier for a 5% increase: 1.051.05
  2. 2
    Apply it once for each year: 1000×1.0531000 × 1.05³
  3. 3
    Work it out: 1000×1.157625=1157.6251000 × 1.157625 = 1157.625, so £1,157.63 to the nearest penny
  4. 4
    Subtract the original amount: 1157.63−1000=157.631157.63 − 1000 = 157.63
Answer
£1,157.63, so the interest earned is £157.63
⚠️ Watch out
1000×0.05×3=£1501000 × 0.05 × 3 = £150 is simple interest. Compound interest is more, because years 2 and 3 earn interest on interest.
Calculate
?£2,500 is invested at 3.2% per year compound interest. Find the amount after 6 years. Give your answer to the nearest penny.
£
Ratio and proportion · growth and decay

Depreciation and repeated changes

  • Depreciation is a loss in value each year. A 15% loss each year means multiplying by 0.850.85 each year.
  • If the rate changes from year to year, use each year's multiplier in turn: ×0.7× 0.7, then ×0.8× 0.8, then ×0.85× 0.85.
  • Never add the percentages: each one is a percentage of the value at the start of that year.
  • A value that keeps falling by a percentage gets smaller every year but never reaches zero.
Quick check
?A car is worth £15,000 when new. It loses 30% of its value in the first year, 20% in the second year and 15% in the third year. What is it worth after 3 years?
Ratio and proportion · growth and decay

Growth and decay formula (Higher)

  • For a percentage change of r%r% each time period, the multiplier is m=1+100r​m = 1 + r/100 (growth) or m=1−100r​m = 1 − r/100 (decay).
  • After nn periods: A=P×mnA = P × mⁿ where PP is the starting amount.
  • A town of 12,000 people growing by 2% a year has about 12000×1.0210≈14,62812000 × 1.02¹⁰ ≈ 14,628 people after 10 years.
  • To find when a value passes a target, try whole values of nn until it does, and interpret the answer in context.
Worked example Ratio and proportion · growth and decay

When does a population fall below a target? (Higher)

Question
A population of 8,000 birds decreases by 4% each year. After how many whole years is it first below 6,000?
  1. 1
    Write the multiplier for a 4% decrease: m=0.96m = 0.96
  2. 2
    Write the formula: population after nn years =8000×0.96n= 8000 × 0.96ⁿ
  3. 3
    Try n=7n = 7: 8000×0.967=6011.68000 × 0.96⁷ = 6011.6, which is not below 6,000
  4. 4
    Try n=8n = 8: 8000×0.968=5771.18000 × 0.96⁸ = 5771.1, which is below 6,000
Answer
after 8 years
⚠️ Watch out
2000÷(4% of 8000)=6.252000 ÷ (4% of 8000) = 6.25 assumes the same 320 birds are lost every year. The yearly loss shrinks as the population shrinks.
Calculate
?Lea has £4,000 to invest for 10 years. Account A pays 2.5% per year compound interest. Account B pays 3% per year simple interest. How much more is the better account worth after 10 years? Give your answer to the nearest penny.
£
Mission check

?£1,000 grows at 5% a year compound interest. When has it first doubled?

After 15 years. Each year multiplies the balance by 1.05, and 1.0514≈1.981.05¹⁴ ≈ 1.98 but 1.0515≈2.081.05¹⁵ ≈ 2.08. Simple interest would take 20 years, because it never pays interest on interest.

Mission 13

4 builders take 6 days. How long would 8 builders take?

Make a guess: 4 builders take 6 days. How long would 8 builders take?

Ratio and proportion · direct and inverse proportion

Direct proportion

  • Two quantities are in direct proportion if multiplying one by a number multiplies the other by the same number: twice the fabric costs twice as much.
  • Unitary method: find the value for one unit, then multiply.
  • The graph of direct proportion is a straight line through the origin.
  • Higher: in algebra, yy is directly proportional to xx, written y∝xy ∝ x, means y=kxy = kx for a constant kk.
Worked example Ratio and proportion · direct and inverse proportion

The unitary method

Question
5 m of fabric costs £32. Find the cost of 8 m of the same fabric.
  1. 1
    Find the cost of one metre: 32÷5=6.4032 ÷ 5 = 6.40, so £6.40 per metre
  2. 2
    Multiply by the number of metres: 6.40×8=51.206.40 × 8 = 51.20
  3. 3
    Check with a scale factor: 88 m is 58​=1.68/5 = 1.6 times as much, and 32×1.6=51.2032 × 1.6 = 51.20
Answer
£51.20
⚠️ Watch out
writing £51.2 loses the mark for money. Give two decimal places.
Ratio and proportion · direct and inverse proportion

Inverse proportion

  • Two quantities are in inverse proportion if multiplying one by a number divides the other by it: double the speed, half the time.
  • Their product stays the same: 60 km/h for 3 hours or 90 km/h for 180÷90=2180 ÷ 90 = 2 hours.
  • Method: multiply to find the fixed total (pump-hours, worker-days), then divide.
  • Higher: in algebra, y∝x1​y ∝ 1/x means y=xk​y = k/x: "yy is proportional to x1​1/x". Its graph is a curve that never meets the axes.
Quick check
?6 identical pumps empty a tank in 10 hours. How long would 4 of these pumps take?
Sort it
?Is yy directly proportional to xx, inversely proportional to xx, or neither?

Tap a statement, then tap the group it belongs in. Then press Check.

Ratio and proportion · direct and inverse proportion

Proportion equations with powers and roots (Higher)

  • Write the statement as an equation with a constant kk: y∝x2y ∝ x² gives y=kx2y = kx²; y∝x​y ∝ √x gives y=kx​y = k√x; y∝x21​y ∝ 1/x² gives y=x2k​y = k/x².
  • Substitute one known pair of values to find kk.
  • Write the equation with that value of kk, then use it to find the unknown.
  • For example, if y∝x​y ∝ √x and y=12y = 12 when x=9x = 9: 12=k×312 = k × 3, so k=4k = 4, and when x=25x = 25, y=4×5=20y = 4 × 5 = 20.
Worked example Ratio and proportion · direct and inverse proportion

Direct proportion to a square (Higher)

Question
yy is directly proportional to x2x². When x=3x = 3, y=45y = 45. Find yy when x=5x = 5.
  1. 1
    Write the equation: y=kx2y = kx²
  2. 2
    Substitute x=3x = 3, y=45y = 45: 45=k×945 = k × 9, so k=5k = 5
  3. 3
    Write the equation with kk: y=5x2y = 5x²
  4. 4
    Substitute x=5x = 5: y=5×25=125y = 5 × 25 = 125
Answer
y=125y = 125
⚠️ Watch out
scaling 4545 by 35​5/3 (to get 75) treats yy as proportional to xx, not to x2x².
Calculate
?The force FF between two small charged spheres is inversely proportional to the square of the distance dd between them. When d=3d = 3, F=20F = 20. Find FF when d=4d = 4. Give your answer as a decimal. (Higher)
Calculate
?A farmer has enough feed to last 12 horses for 15 days. She buys 3 more horses. Each horse eats the same amount each day. How many days will the feed now last?
days
Mission check

?4 builders take 6 days to build a wall. How long would 8 builders take?

The wall is 4×6=244 × 6 = 24 builder-days of work, so 8 builders need 24÷8=324 ÷ 8 = 3 days. That is the inverse proportion model. On a real site it only holds if every builder works at the same rate and nobody waits for anyone else; some jobs (like concrete setting) take the same time however many people help.

Mission 14

A 1 m by 1 m by 1 m tank is full of water. Could two people lift it?

Make a guess: A 1 m by 1 m by 1 m tank is full of water. Could two people lift it?

Measures · compound measures and units

Converting area and volume units

  • Length: 1 m=100 cm1 m = 100 cm, 1 cm=10 mm1 cm = 10 mm, 1 km=1000 m1 km = 1000 m.
  • Area: square the length factor. A 1 m square is 100 cm by 100 cm, so 1 m2=1002=10,000 cm21 m² = 100² = 10,000 cm².
  • Volume: cube the length factor. 1 m3=1003 cm31 m³ = 100³ cm³, and 1 cm3=1000 mm31 cm³ = 1000 mm³.
  • Capacity: 1 litre=1000 cm31 litre = 1000 cm³ and 1 ml=1 cm31 ml = 1 cm³.
  • Know the common approximate equivalents: 1 inch ≈ 2.5 cm, 5 miles ≈ 8 km, 1 kg ≈ 2.2 pounds, 1 gallon ≈ 4.5 litres.
Quick check
?Convert 3.5 m23.5 m² to cm2cm².
Measures · compound measures and units

Speed, distance and time

  • speed=timedistance​speed = distance/time so distance == speed × time and time == distance ÷ speed. Average speed == total distance ÷ total time.
  • Minutes ÷ 60 gives hours: 2 h 15 min =2.25= 2.25 h. 0.4 h =0.4×60=24= 0.4 × 60 = 24 min.
  • 72 km/h72 km/h is 72,00072,000 m in 3,600 s, which is 20 m/s20 m/s.
  • 24-hour clock 15 15 is 3.15 pm on the 12-hour clock.
Worked example Measures · compound measures and units

Average speed with hours and minutes

Question
A cyclist rides 54 km in 2 hours 15 minutes. Find her average speed in km/h.
  1. 1
    Change the time to hours: 15÷60=0.2515 ÷ 60 = 0.25, so the time is 2.252.25 hours
  2. 2
    Use speed == distance ÷ time: 54÷2.2554 ÷ 2.25
  3. 3
    Work it out: 54÷2.25=2454 ÷ 2.25 = 24
Answer
24 km/h
⚠️ Watch out
typing 2 h 15 min as 2.15 gives 54÷2.15≈25.1254 ÷ 2.15 ≈ 25.12 km/h. 15 minutes is 0.25 of an hour, not 0.15.
Calculate
?A train leaves at 09 47 and travels 168 km at an average speed of 96 km/h. How many minutes does the journey take?
minutes
Measures · compound measures and units

Density, pressure and other rates

  • density=volumemass​density = mass/volume in g/cm³ or kg/m³.
  • pressure=areaforce​pressure = force/area in newtons per square metre (N/m²), also called pascals (Pa).
  • Higher: pressure is Higher tier only; density is on both tiers.
  • Other rates work the same way: pay per hour, cost per kg, litres per minute (flow rate), km per litre (fuel use), people per km² (population density).
Worked example Measures · compound measures and units

Finding a density

Question
A metal block measures 5 cm by 4 cm by 2 cm. Its mass is 316 g. Find the density of the metal.
  1. 1
    Find the volume: 5×4×2=40 cm35 × 4 × 2 = 40 cm³
  2. 2
    Use density == mass ÷ volume: 316÷40316 ÷ 40
  3. 3
    Work it out: 316÷40=7.9316 ÷ 40 = 7.9
Answer
7.9 g/cm37.9 g/cm³
⚠️ Watch out
the units come from the division: grams ÷ cm³ gives g/cm³. Dividing volume by mass gives a number with no meaning here.
Calculate
?A water tank is a cuboid 1.2 m long, 0.8 m wide and 0.5 m deep. It is empty. Water flows in at 8 litres per minute. How many minutes does it take to fill the tank?
minutes
Calculate
?Oak has a density of 0.75 g/cm30.75 g/cm³. An oak plank is 2 m long, 20 cm wide and 3 cm thick. Find its mass in kg.
kg
Mission check

?A 1 m by 1 m by 1 m tank is full of water (1 cm³ of water has a mass of about 1 g). Could two people lift it?

No. The tank holds 100×100×100=1,000,000 cm3100 × 100 × 100 = 1,000,000 cm³ of water, which is 1,000 litres. At about 1 g per cm³ that is about 1,000 kg (one tonne): far too heavy for two people to lift.

Ratio · proportion in everyday life

Best buys

  • To find the best buy, compare the same unit: price per gram, or grams per penny.
  • Convert first so the units match: 1.2 kg = 1200 g; 500 ml = 0.5 L.
  • Compare what you actually get. For pizzas that is area, πr2π r², not diameter.
  • A 10 cm pizza has area π×52≈79π × 5² ≈ 79 cm². A 30 cm pizza has π×152≈707π × 15² ≈ 707 cm², 9 times as much: triple the width, nine times the pizza.
Worked example Ratio · proportion in everyday life

Which pack is better value?

Question
Cereal comes in 750 g for £2.85 or 1.2 kg for £4.20. Which is better value?
  1. 1
    Use the same units: 1.2 kg = 1200 g, £2.85 = 285p, £4.20 = 420p
  2. 2
    Price per gram, small pack: 285÷750=0.38285 ÷ 750 = 0.38p per g
  3. 3
    Price per gram, large pack: 420÷1200=0.35420 ÷ 1200 = 0.35p per g
  4. 4
    Compare: the lower price per gram is better value
Answer
The 1.2 kg pack is better value (0.35p per g against 0.38p per g).
⚠️ Watch out
say which unit you compared. If you work out grams per penny instead, the bigger number wins.
Quick check
?Juice is sold as 1.5 L for £1.80, 2 L for £2.30 or 500 ml for £0.65. Which is the best value?
Ratio · proportion in everyday life

Recipes and exchange rates

  • Quantities in direct proportion keep the same ratio. Scale them by one multiplier.
  • Unitary method: find one, then multiply. A recipe for 6 needs 450 g flour; for 1 person, 75 g; for 4 people, 300 g.
  • An exchange rate is a multiplier. If £1 = €1.15, multiply pounds by 1.15 to get euros, and divide euros by 1.15 to get pounds.
  • Sense-check: you should get more euros than pounds at this rate.
Calculate
?Exam-style. A recipe for 8 people needs 600 g of flour and 4 eggs. Ana has 1 kg of flour and 5 eggs. What is the greatest number of people she can make the recipe for?
Calculate
?Exam-style. Sam changes £400 to euros when £1 = €1.15. Sam spends €385 on holiday, then changes the euros left back to pounds when £1 = €1.25. How many pounds does Sam get back?
£
Ratio · proportion in everyday life

Map scales

  • A map scale 1 : 25,000 means 1 cm on the map is 25,000 cm in real life.
  • Change units: 25,000 cm = 250 m, so 4 cm on the map is 1 km.
  • Map to real: multiply by 25,000. Real to map: divide by 25,000. Change the units at the end (100 cm = 1 m, 100,000 cm = 1 km).
  • Higher: areas scale by the square. 1 cm² on this map is 250 m × 250 m = 62,500 m².
Calculate
?A walking map has scale 1 : 25,000. Two farms are 7.4 cm apart on the map. How far apart are they in real life, in kilometres?
km

Mission check

?A 20 cm pizza costs £6 and a 40 cm pizza costs £18. Is the large pizza a good deal?

Yes, it is a good deal. Doubling the diameter multiplies the area by 4, so you get 4 times the pizza for 3 times the price: about 70 cm² per pound, against about 52 cm² per pound for the small one.

Algebra · expressions

Terms, expressions and like terms

  • An expression is a collection of terms such as 5a5a, −9b−9b or x2x². The number in front of a letter is its coefficient.
  • Algebra shorthand: abab means a×ba × b, 3y3y means y+y+yy + y + y, a2ba²b means a×a×ba × a × b, ba​a/b means a÷ba ÷ b.
  • Like terms have exactly the same letters and powers. Collect them by adding their coefficients: 2a+3b+5a−9b=7a−6b2a + 3b + 5a − 9b = 7a − 6b.
  • x2x² and xx are not like terms: 3x2+2x3x² + 2x cannot be simplified.
  • To expand a single bracket, multiply every term inside by the term outside: 3x(2x−4y)=6x2−12xy3x(2x − 4y) = 6x² − 12xy and −4(x−3)=−4x+12−4(x − 3) = −4x + 12.
Quick check
?Expand and simplify 3(2x−1)−2(x−4)3(2x − 1) − 2(x − 4).
Algebra · expressions

Expanding two brackets

  • Multiply every term in the first bracket by every term in the second. A grid keeps track: four boxes, four products.
  • (x+5)(x+2)(x + 5)(x + 2): the boxes are x2x², 2x2x, 5x5x and 1010. Collect the like terms: x2+7x+10x² + 7x + 10.
  • The grid is also an area picture: a rectangle (x+5)(x + 5) by (x+2)(x + 2) splits into four smaller rectangles.
  • Higher: for CCEA, multiplying two linear expressions is Higher tier (Unit M3).
Worked example Algebra · expressions

Expanding and simplifying two brackets (Higher)

Question
Expand and simplify (2x+1)(x−4)(2x + 1)(x − 4).
  1. 1
    Multiply the first terms: 2x×x=2x22x × x = 2x²
  2. 2
    Multiply the outer and inner pairs: 2x×(−4)=−8x2x × (−4) = −8x and 1×x=x1 × x = x
  3. 3
    Multiply the last terms: 1×(−4)=−41 × (−4) = −4
  4. 4
    Collect the like terms: −8x+x=−7x−8x + x = −7x
Answer
2x2−7x−42x² − 7x − 4
⚠️ Watch out
the sign belongs to the term after it. The −4−4 in the second bracket makes two of the four products negative.
Calculate
?Expand (x−6)2(x − 6)² and write it in the form x2+bx+cx² + bx + c. Enter the value of bb (exact).
Algebra · expressions

Factorising: expanding in reverse

  • Factorise means write as a product. Take out the highest common factor of every term: 9x2+15xy=3x(3x+5y)9x² + 15xy = 3x(3x + 5y). "Factorise fully" means nothing more can come out.
  • A quadratic x2+bx+cx² + bx + c factorises to (x+p)(x+q)(x + p)(x + q) where pp and qq multiply to cc and add to bb: x2+7x+10=(x+5)(x+2)x² + 7x + 10 = (x + 5)(x + 2).
  • Difference of two squares: x2−a2=(x−a)(x+a)x² − a² = (x − a)(x + a), so x2−16=(x−4)(x+4)x² − 16 = (x − 4)(x + 4).
  • Check any factorisation by expanding it again.
  • Higher: for CCEA, factorising quadratics and the difference of two squares are Higher tier (Units M3 and M4).
Quick check
?Factorise x2+2x−24x² + 2x − 24.
Worked example Algebra · expressions

Factorising ax2+bx+cax² + bx + c (Higher)

Question
Factorise 6x2−5x−66x² − 5x − 6.
  1. 1
    Multiply aa by cc: 6×(−6)=−366 × (−6) = −36
  2. 2
    Find two numbers that multiply to −36−36 and add to −5−5: −9−9 and 44
  3. 3
    Split the middle term with them: 6x2−9x+4x−66x² − 9x + 4x − 6
  4. 4
    Factorise each pair: 3x(2x−3)+2(2x−3)3x(2x − 3) + 2(2x − 3)
  5. 5
    Take out the common bracket: (2x−3)(3x+2)(2x − 3)(3x + 2)
Answer
(2x−3)(3x+2)(2x − 3)(3x + 2)
⚠️ Watch out
check by expanding. (2x−3)(3x+2)=6x2+4x−9x−6=6x2−5x−6(2x − 3)(3x + 2) = 6x² + 4x − 9x − 6 = 6x² − 5x − 6.
Calculate
?A square photo of side xx cm sits in a square frame of side (x+4)(x + 4) cm. The visible frame (the outer square minus the photo) has an area of 200 cm². Form an expression for the frame's area, simplify it, and find xx (exact).
Mission check

?A square photo of side xx cm is made 3 cm wider and 3 cm taller. Which expression gives its new area in cm²?

The bigger square splits into four pieces: the old x2x², two strips of 3x3x and a 3 by 3 corner. So the area is x2+6x+9x² + 6x + 9, not x2+9x² + 9. In general (a+b)2=a2+2ab+b2(a + b)² = a² + 2ab + b²: the 2ab2ab is the two strips.

Algebra · formulae

Expressions, equations, formulae

  • An expression has no equals sign: 3x+53x + 5.
  • An equation is true only for particular values of the letter: 3x+5=203x + 5 = 20 is true only when x=5x = 5.
  • A formula links two or more quantities, so you can work one out from the others: v=u+atv = u + at.
  • Higher: an identity is true for every value of the letter. It is often written with ≡≡: 2(x+3)≡2x+62(x + 3) ≡ 2x + 6.
Sort it
?Sort each line into the right group.

Tap a statement, then tap the group it belongs in. Then press Check.

Algebra · formulae

Substituting into formulae

  • Substitute means replace each letter by its value, then follow the order of operations: brackets, powers, then ×× and ÷÷, then ++ and −−.
  • Put negative numbers in brackets: if x=−3x = −3, then x2=(−3)2=9x² = (−3)² = 9 and 2x2=2×9=182x² = 2 × 9 = 18.
  • Watch the minus: 5−2x=5−2×(−3)=5+6=115 − 2x = 5 − 2 × (−3) = 5 + 6 = 11.
  • A formula in words works the same way: write it with letters first, then substitute.
Worked example Algebra · formulae

Substituting into a kinematics formula

Question
Use s=ut+21​at2s = ut + 1/2at² to find ss when u=12u = 12, t=3t = 3 and a=−4a = −4.
  1. 1
    Substitute, keeping the negative in brackets: s=12×3+21​×(−4)×32s = 12 × 3 + 1/2 × (−4) × 3²
  2. 2
    Work out the power first: 32=93² = 9
  3. 3
    Work out each product: 12×3=3612 × 3 = 36 and 21​×(−4)×9=−181/2 × (−4) × 9 = −18
  4. 4
    Add: 36+(−18)=1836 + (−18) = 18
Answer
s=18s = 18
⚠️ Watch out
only tt is squared. Squaring atat gives 21​×144=721/2 × 144 = 72 and the wrong answer 108.
Calculate
?The formula F=1.8C+32F = 1.8C + 32 converts a temperature CC in °C to FF in °F. Find FF when C=−25C = −25 (exact).
Algebra · formulae

Changing the subject

  • The subject is the letter on its own on one side, like vv in v=u+atv = u + at.
  • To change the subject, undo the operations on the letter you want, in reverse order, doing the same to both sides.
  • v=u+atv = u + at: subtract uu, then divide by aa, so t=av−u​t = (v − u)/a.
  • y=3x−2y = 3x − 2: add 2, then divide by 3, so x=3y+2​x = (y + 2)/3.
  • Higher: if the subject is squared, undo the square last with a square root: A=πr2A = π r² gives r=πA​​r = √(A/π).
Worked example Algebra · formulae

Rearranging the temperature formula

Question
Make CC the subject of F=59C​+32F = 9C/5 + 32.
  1. 1
    Subtract 32 from both sides: F−32=59C​F − 32 = 9C/5
  2. 2
    Multiply both sides by 5: 5(F−32)=9C5(F − 32) = 9C
  3. 3
    Divide both sides by 9: C=95(F−32)​C = (5(F − 32))/9
  4. 4
    Check with a known value: F=212F = 212 gives C=95×180​=100C = (5 × 180)/9 = 100
Answer
C=95(F−32)​C = (5(F − 32))/9
⚠️ Watch out
the bracket matters. 95F−32​(5F − 32)/9 subtracts 32 after multiplying by 5, which is a different formula.
Worked example Algebra · formulae

When the subject appears twice (Higher)

Question
Make xx the subject of ax+5=3x+bax + 5 = 3x + b.
  1. 1
    Get every xx term on one side, everything else on the other: ax−3x=b−5ax − 3x = b − 5
  2. 2
    Factorise out xx: x(a−3)=b−5x(a − 3) = b − 5
  3. 3
    Divide by the bracket: x=a−3b−5​x = (b − 5)/(a − 3)
  4. 4
    Check with numbers, e.g. a=7a = 7, b=13b = 13: x=2x = 2, and 7×2+5=19=3×2+137 × 2 + 5 = 19 = 3 × 2 + 13
Answer
x=a−3b−5​x = (b − 5)/(a − 3)
⚠️ Watch out
you can't divide by aa and by 3 separately. Collect the xx terms, then factorise: that is the only way to get one xx.
Calculate
?A taxi charges a fixed £3.50 plus £1.80 for every mile. Write a formula for the cost CC (in £) of a journey of mm miles. A journey costs £26. How many miles was it? Give your answer as a decimal.
miles
Mission check

?Is there one temperature that reads the same in °C and °F? Use F=1.8C+32F = 1.8C + 32.

Set the two readings equal: C=1.8C+32C = 1.8C + 32. Subtract 1.8C1.8C: −0.8C=32−0.8C = 32, so C=−40C = −40. At −40 the scales agree; it is the only temperature where they do.

Algebra · linear equations and inequalities

Solving linear equations

  • Keep the equation balanced: whatever you do to one side, do to the other.
  • Brackets: expand them first. 7(x+3)=5x−87(x + 3) = 5x − 8 becomes 7x+21=5x−87x + 21 = 5x − 8.
  • Unknown on both sides: subtract the smaller xx term from both sides so xx appears once: 2x+21=−82x + 21 = −8, so x=−14.5x = −14.5.
  • Fractions: multiply every term by the denominator: 24x+5​=3(4x + 5)/2 = 3 gives 4x+5=64x + 5 = 6, so x=0.25x = 0.25.
Worked example Algebra · linear equations and inequalities

Brackets and the unknown on both sides

Question
Solve 5(x−1)=4−x5(x − 1) = 4 − x.
  1. 1
    Expand the bracket: 5x−5=4−x5x − 5 = 4 − x
  2. 2
    Add xx to both sides: 6x−5=46x − 5 = 4
  3. 3
    Add 5 to both sides: 6x=96x = 9
  4. 4
    Divide both sides by 6: x=1.5x = 1.5
Answer
x=1.5x = 1.5
⚠️ Watch out
check by substituting. 5(1.5−1)=2.55(1.5 − 1) = 2.5 and 4−1.5=2.54 − 1.5 = 2.5, so both sides agree.
Algebra · linear equations and inequalities

Forming an equation from words

  • Choose a letter for the unknown and say what it stands for: "let mm be the number of months".
  • Write each quantity as an expression in that letter. A fixed charge plus a rate per unit is "fixed + rate × units".
  • When two quantities are equal, write expression = expression and solve.
  • Finish by answering the question asked, in context and with units.
Worked example Algebra · linear equations and inequalities

When do two costs match?

Question
Gym A charges £60 to join plus £15 a month. Gym B has no joining fee and charges £27 a month. After how many months is the total cost the same?
  1. 1
    Let mm be the number of months. Gym A costs 60+15m60 + 15m and gym B costs 27m27m.
  2. 2
    Set the costs equal: 60+15m=27m60 + 15m = 27m
  3. 3
    Subtract 15m15m from both sides: 60=12m60 = 12m
  4. 4
    Divide by 12: m=5m = 5
Answer
after 5 months (both cost £135). After that, gym A is cheaper, because it adds less each month.
⚠️ Watch out
the question asks for months, so "m=5m = 5" alone is not the full answer. Say what it means.
Calculate

cm
Algebra · linear equations and inequalities

Linear inequalities

  • << less than, >> greater than, ≤≤ at most, ≥≥ at least.
  • Number line: open circle for << or >> (end value not included), closed circle for ≤≤ or ≥≥.
  • Solve an inequality like an equation: 3x−2<103x − 2 < 10 gives 3x<123x < 12, so x<4x < 4.
  • If you multiply or divide by a negative number, reverse the inequality sign: −2x<6−2x < 6 gives x>−3x > −3.
Calculate

Algebra · linear equations and inequalities

Regions on a graph (Higher)

  • An inequality in xx and yy, such as x+y≤5x + y ≤ 5, describes a region of the grid.
  • Draw the boundary line x+y=5x + y = 5: solid for ≤≤ or ≥≥, dashed for << or >>.
  • Test a point not on the line, such as (0,0)(0, 0): 0+0≤50 + 0 ≤ 5 is true, so the region is on the side containing (0,0)(0, 0).
  • Several inequalities together give the region where all are true.

?Plan A costs £12 a month plus £0.08 a minute. Plan B costs £20 a month plus £0.03 a minute. When is Plan B cheaper?

Write each bill in pounds: 12+0.08m12 + 0.08m and 20+0.03m20 + 0.03m. They are equal when 0.05m=80.05m = 8, so m=160m = 160 (both £24.80). Plan B is cheaper when 20+0.03m<12+0.08m20 + 0.03m < 12 + 0.08m, which is m>160m > 160: at 200 minutes B costs £26 and A costs £28.

Rise 1 for every 12 along: which of three ramps is legal?

Algebra · straight-line graphs

Gradient measures steepness

  • Gradient = change in yy ÷ change in xx ("rise over run").
m=x2​−x1​y2​−y1​​m = (y₂ − y₁)/(x₂ − x₁)
  • Uphill from left to right: positive. Downhill: negative. Horizontal: 0.
  • The bigger the gradient (ignoring its sign), the steeper the line.
  • "Rise 1 for every 12 along" is a gradient of 121​1/12.
Algebra · straight-line graphs

The equation y=mx+cy = mx + c

  • In y=mx+cy = mx + c, mm is the gradient and cc is the yy-intercept: the line crosses the yy-axis at (0,c)(0, c).
  • Rearrange to y=…y = … first: 2y=6x−42y = 6x − 4 gives y=3x−2y = 3x − 2, so m=3m = 3 and c=−2c = −2.
  • To plot: make a table of values (three or more xx values), plot the points, rule the line.
  • y=ky = k is a horizontal line; x=kx = k is a vertical line.
  • CCEA: gradients and intercepts from a graph are Foundation (M2); y=mx+cy = mx + c and line equations are Higher (M3).
Quick check
?What is the gradient of the line 2y=12−3x2y = 12 − 3x?
Worked example Algebra · straight-line graphs

Equation of the line through two points

Question
Find the equation of the line through (2,7)(2, 7) and (5,13)(5, 13).
  1. 1
    Find the gradient: m=5−213−7​=36​=2m = (13 − 7)/(5 − 2) = 6/3 = 2
  2. 2
    Substitute one point into y=2x+cy = 2x + c: 7=2×2+c7 = 2 × 2 + c
  3. 3
    Solve for cc: c=3c = 3
  4. 4
    Check with the other point: 2×5+3=132 × 5 + 3 = 13 ✓
Answer
y=2x+3y = 2x + 3
⚠️ Watch out
subtract the coordinates in the same order on the top and the bottom, or the sign of the gradient flips.
Calculate
?A taxi fare is a fixed charge plus a set amount per mile, so fare against miles is a straight line. A 3-mile trip costs £8.40 and an 8-mile trip costs £15.40. Find the fixed charge. Give your answer as a decimal.
£
Algebra · straight-line graphs

Parallel and perpendicular lines

  • Parallel lines have equal gradients. The line parallel to y=4x−1y = 4x − 1 through (1,−3)(1, −3): −3=4×1+c−3 = 4 × 1 + c, so y=4x−7y = 4x − 7.
  • Higher: perpendicular lines have gradients that multiply to −1−1. Use the negative reciprocal: gradient 2 becomes −21​−1/2.
  • Higher: 2y=3x+12y = 3x + 1 has gradient 23​3/2, so a perpendicular line has gradient −32​−2/3.
  • For CCEA (Unit M3) and Edexcel IGCSE, parallel lines are Higher tier content too.
Calculate
?(Higher) Line LL has equation y=2x+5y = 2x + 5. Line MM is perpendicular to LL and passes through (4,1)(4, 1). Find the yy-intercept of line MM.
Algebra · straight-line graphs

Midpoint and length of a line segment

  • The midpoint averages the coordinates:
(2x1​+x2​​,2y1​+y2​​)((x₁ + x₂)/2, (y₁ + y₂)/2)
  • The length comes from Pythagoras: (x2​−x1​)2+(y2​−y1​)2​√((x₂ − x₁)² + (y₂ − y₁)²).
  • For A(1,2)A(1, 2) and B(7,10)B(7, 10): the midpoint is (4,6)(4, 6) and the length is 62+82​=10√(6² + 8²) = 10.
Calculate
?Point PP is (−3,8)(−3, 8) and point QQ is (9,−2)(9, −2). Find the length of PQPQ. Give your answer to 3 significant figures.
Mission check

?The rule: no steeper than a rise of 1 for every 12 along. Ramp P rises 0.6 m over 9 m, ramp Q is the line y=0.1xy = 0.1x, ramp R rises 0.25 m over 3 m. Which ramps are legal?

Steepness is measured by gradient, rise ÷ run. The rule allows a gradient up to 121​≈0.0831/12 ≈ 0.083: ramp P (about 0.067) and ramp R (exactly 121​1/12) pass, but ramp Q, with m=0.1m = 0.1 in y=0.1xy = 0.1x, is too steep.

A thrown ball is 10 m up at two different times. When, and why?

Algebra · quadratic equations

Solving by factorising

  • Make one side 0: write the equation as ax2+bx+c=0ax² + bx + c = 0.
  • Factorise, then use: if AB=0AB = 0, then A=0A = 0 or B=0B = 0.
  • Each bracket gives one root, so there are usually two solutions.
  • The roots are where the graph of y=ax2+bx+cy = ax² + bx + c crosses the xx-axis; a graph gives approximate solutions.
  • CCEA: solving by factorising is Higher (Unit M3). Foundation finds approximate solutions from a graph (Unit M6).
Worked example Algebra · quadratic equations

Solving x2+2x−15=0x² + 2x − 15 = 0 (Higher)

Question
Solve x2+2x−15=0x² + 2x − 15 = 0.
  1. 1
    Find two numbers that multiply to −15−15 and add to 22: they are 55 and −3−3
  2. 2
    Factorise: (x+5)(x−3)=0(x + 5)(x − 3) = 0
  3. 3
    Set each bracket equal to zero: x+5=0x + 5 = 0 or x−3=0x − 3 = 0
Answer
x=−5x = −5 or x=3x = 3
⚠️ Watch out
x+5=0x + 5 = 0 gives x=−5x = −5, not 55. Each root has the opposite sign to the number in its bracket.

Algebra · quadratic equations

The quadratic formula (Higher)

  • For ax2+bx+c=0ax² + bx + c = 0:
x=2a−b±b2−4ac​​x = (−b ± √(b² − 4ac))/2a
  • Use it when the quadratic does not factorise, or when you need decimals or surds.
  • Rearrange to …=0… = 0 first, and take each of aa, bb, cc with its sign.
  • If b2−4acb² − 4ac is negative there are no solutions: the graph does not cross the xx-axis.
  • CCEA uses it when the coefficient of x2x² is not 1 (Unit M4). Check your board's formula sheet to see whether it is printed; if not, learn it.
Worked example Algebra · quadratic equations

Using the formula (Higher)

Question
Solve 2x2−3x−4=02x² − 3x − 4 = 0. Give your answers to 2 decimal places.
  1. 1
    Identify the coefficients: a=2a = 2, b=−3b = −3, c=−4c = −4
  2. 2
    Work out b2−4ac=(−3)2−4×2×(−4)=9+32=41b² − 4ac = (−3)² − 4 × 2 × (−4) = 9 + 32 = 41
  3. 3
    Substitute: x=43±41​​x = (3 ± √41)/4
  4. 4
    Evaluate each sign: 43+6.403…​(3 + 6.403…)/4 and 43−6.403…​(3 − 6.403…)/4
Answer
x=2.35x = 2.35 or x=−0.85x = −0.85
⚠️ Watch out
−b−b is +3+3 here because b=−3b = −3; and (−3)2=9(−3)² = 9, not −9−9.

Mission check

?A ball's height after tt seconds is h=15t−5t2h = 15t − 5t² metres. It is 10 m up when 5t2−15t+10=05t² − 15t + 10 = 0. When is the ball 10 m up?

Divide by 5 and factorise: t2−3t+2=(t−1)(t−2)=0t² − 3t + 2 = (t − 1)(t − 2) = 0, so t=1t = 1 or t=2t = 2. The quadratic has two roots because the ball goes up and comes back down: it passes 10 m after 1 s on the way up and after 2 s on the way down.

Mission 21

3 coffees + 2 cakes = £13.50; 2 coffees + 3 cakes = £13. A cake?

Make a guess: 3 coffees + 2 cakes = £13.50; 2 coffees + 3 cakes = £13. A cake?

Algebra · simultaneous equations

Two unknowns, two equations

  • One equation in xx and yy has endless solutions. Simultaneous equations are two equations that must both be true at once.
  • The solution is the pair xx, yy that fits both.
  • Graphically, each linear equation is a line; the solution is where the lines intersect. y=2x−1y = 2x − 1 and x+y=5x + y = 5 meet at (2,3)(2, 3).
  • Always check your pair in both original equations.
  • CCEA: Foundation solves these graphically (Unit M6); solving algebraically is Higher (Unit M7).
Worked example Algebra · simultaneous equations

Solving by elimination (Higher)

Question
Solve 3x+2y=163x + 2y = 16 and 5x−3y=145x − 3y = 14.
  1. 1
    Match the yy coefficients: multiply the first by 3 and the second by 2: 9x+6y=489x + 6y = 48 and 10x−6y=2810x − 6y = 28
  2. 2
    The signs of 6y6y differ, so add: 19x=7619x = 76
  3. 3
    Divide: x=4x = 4
  4. 4
    Substitute into 3x+2y=163x + 2y = 16: 12+2y=1612 + 2y = 16, so y=2y = 2
  5. 5
    Check in the other equation: 5×4−3×2=145 × 4 − 3 × 2 = 14 ✓
Answer
x=4x = 4, y=2y = 2
⚠️ Watch out
add when the matched terms have different signs and subtract when they have the same sign. Multiply every term, including the number on the right.
Quick check
?Solve 5x+2y=205x + 2y = 20 and 3x−2y=43x − 2y = 4.
Algebra · simultaneous equations

Solving by substitution (Higher)

  • Use substitution when one equation already says y=…y = … or x=…x = ….
  • Replace that letter in the other equation, using brackets: y=2x−1y = 2x − 1 into x+y=5x + y = 5 gives x+(2x−1)=5x + (2x − 1) = 5.
  • Solve for one letter: 3x=63x = 6, so x=2x = 2; then y=2×2−1=3y = 2 × 2 − 1 = 3.
  • Elimination and substitution give the same answer; pick whichever is quicker.

Algebra · simultaneous equations

One linear, one quadratic (Higher)

  • Rearrange the linear equation to y=…y = … (or x=…x = …) and substitute it into the quadratic one.
  • You get a quadratic equation in one letter: make it =0= 0 and solve.
  • Find the partner value for each root using the linear equation. Give the answers as pairs.
  • A line can meet a curve at two points, one point (it touches) or no points.
  • The curve might be a circle such as x2+y2=25x² + y² = 25: the same method works.
Worked example Algebra · simultaneous equations

A line meeting a curve (Higher)

Question
Solve y=2x+1y = 2x + 1 and y=x2−2y = x² − 2.
  1. 1
    Set the two expressions for yy equal: x2−2=2x+1x² − 2 = 2x + 1
  2. 2
    Make one side zero: x2−2x−3=0x² − 2x − 3 = 0
  3. 3
    Factorise: (x−3)(x+1)=0(x − 3)(x + 1) = 0, so x=3x = 3 or x=−1x = −1
  4. 4
    Use y=2x+1y = 2x + 1 for each: y=7y = 7 or y=−1y = −1
Answer
x=3,y=7x = 3, y = 7 and x=−1,y=−1x = −1, y = −1
⚠️ Watch out

Mission check

?3 coffees and 2 cakes cost £13.50. 2 coffees and 3 cakes cost £13.00. How much is one cake?

Write 3f+2k=13.503f + 2k = 13.50 and 2f+3k=132f + 3k = 13. Adding gives 5f+5k=26.505f + 5k = 26.50, so f+k=5.30f + k = 5.30; subtracting gives f−k=0.50f − k = 0.50. So a coffee is £2.90 and a cake is £2.40: two equations pin down two unknowns.

Mission 22

Four graphs, four equations: can you match them without plotting?

Make a guess: Four graphs, four equations: can you match them without plotting?

Algebra · graphs of functions

Lines and parabolas

  • A linear graph y=mx+cy=mx+c is a straight line: gradient mm, crossing the yy-axis at (0,c)(0, c).
  • A quadratic graph y=ax2+bx+cy=ax²+bx+c is a parabola: U-shaped if a>0a>0, ∩-shaped if a<0a<0.
  • The roots are where the curve crosses the xx-axis (y=0y=0). The yy-intercept is at (0,c)(0, c).
  • The turning point lies on the line of symmetry, halfway between the roots.
Worked example Algebra · graphs of functions

Reading a quadratic graph

Question
The graph of y=x2−2x−3y = x² − 2x − 3 is drawn. Find its roots, its turning point, and use it to solve x2−2x−3=5x² − 2x − 3 = 5.
  1. 1
    Read where the curve crosses the xx-axis: x=−1x = −1 and x=3x = 3
  2. 2
    The line of symmetry is halfway between: x=2−1+3​=1x = (−1+3)/2 = 1
  3. 3
    Substitute x=1x = 1: y=1−2−3=−4y = 1 − 2 − 3 = −4, so the turning point is (1,−4)(1, −4)
  4. 4
    Draw the line y=5y = 5 and read where it meets the curve: x=−2x = −2 and x=4x = 4
Answer
roots x=−1x = −1 and x=3x = 3; turning point (1,−4)(1, −4); solutions x=−2x = −2 or x=4x = 4
⚠️ Watch out
to solve x2−2x−3=5x² − 2x − 3 = 5 you read off at y=5y = 5, not at y=0y = 0.
Calculate
?The graph of y=x2+2x−8y = x² + 2x − 8 is drawn for −6≤x≤4−6 ≤ x ≤ 4. Use the graph to solve x2+2x−8=7x² + 2x − 8 = 7. Enter the positive solution.
Algebra · graphs of functions

Cubics and reciprocals

  • A cubic y=ax3+…y=ax³+… is S-shaped: rising left to right if a>0a>0, falling if a<0a<0. y=x3−4xy = x³ − 4x has roots −2−2, 0 and 2.
  • The reciprocal graph y=xa​y=a/x has two branches that never touch the axes (the asymptotes); x=0x ≠ 0.
  • To match an equation to a graph: check the highest power of xx and its sign, then the intercepts.
  • On your course cubic and reciprocal graphs are Higher tier.

Algebra · graphs of functions

Exponential graphs (Higher)

  • An exponential graph y=kxy = k^x (k>0k > 0) always passes through (0,1)(0, 1), because k0=1k⁰ = 1.
  • If k>1k > 1 it shows growth: y=2xy = 2^x goes 1, 2, 4, 8 as xx goes 0, 1, 2, 3.
  • If 0<k<10 < k < 1 it shows decay: y=(21​)xy = (1/2)^x falls towards 0.
  • It never touches the xx-axis: y=0y=0 is an asymptote, and yy is always positive.
Mission check

?Four graphs, four equations. Graph P has two separate branches and never meets either axis. Which equation matches it, and why?

Yes, you can match them without plotting. The highest power of xx and its sign fix the shape (line, parabola, cubic, or reciprocal), and the intercepts confirm it. Only y=x4​y = 4/x avoids both axes.

Mission 23

Chessboard: 1 grain, then double each square. How many on square 64?

Make a guess: Chessboard: 1 grain, then double each square. How many on square 64?

Algebra · sequences

Two kinds of rule

  • A term-to-term rule gets each term from the one before: 5, 9, 13, 17, … is "add 4".
  • A position-to-term rule (the nth term) gets any term from its position nn: here 4n+14n + 1.
  • Substitute nn to find a term: the 10th term is 4×10+1=414 × 10 + 1 = 41.
  • The chessboard has term-to-term rule "double".
Worked example Algebra · sequences

Finding the nth term of a linear sequence

Question
Find the nth term of 7, 10, 13, 16, … and its 100th term. Is 100 a term?
  1. 1
    Find the common difference: 10−7=310 − 7 = 3, so the nth term starts 3n3n
  2. 2
    Compare with 3n3n (3, 6, 9, 12): each term is 4 more, so add 4
  3. 3
    Write the rule: nth term =3n+4= 3n + 4
  4. 4
    Substitute n=100n = 100: 3×100+4=3043 × 100 + 4 = 304
  5. 5
    Solve 3n+4=1003n + 4 = 100: n=32n = 32, a whole number, so 100 is the 32nd term
Answer
nth term 3n+43n + 4; 100th term 304; 100 is a term (the 32nd).
⚠️ Watch out
the nth term is not "n+3n + 3". The difference 3 multiplies nn.
Calculate

Calculate

Algebra · sequences

Special sequences

  • Square numbers n2n²: 1, 4, 9, 16, … and cube numbers n3n³: 1, 8, 27, 64, ….
  • Triangular numbers: 1, 3, 6, 10, 15, … (add 2, then 3, then 4, …).
  • A geometric sequence multiplies by the same number rr each time: 3, 6, 12, 24 (r=2r = 2). The chessboard 1, 2, 4, 8, … is geometric: square nn holds 2n−12ⁿ⁻¹.

Algebra · sequences

The nth term of a quadratic sequence (Higher)

  • If the second differences are constant, the nth term is an2+bn+can² + bn + c.
  • The coefficient of n2n² is half the second difference.
  • Subtract an2an² from each term. What is left is linear: find its nth term and add it on.
Worked example Algebra · sequences

Quadratic nth term (Higher)

Question
Find the nth term of 4, 11, 22, 37, ….
  1. 1
    First differences: 7, 11, 15. Second differences: 4, 4, so it is quadratic
  2. 2
    Halve the second difference: 24​=24/2 = 2, so it starts 2n22n²
  3. 3
    Subtract 2n22n² (2, 8, 18, 32) from each term: 2, 3, 4, 5
  4. 4
    The leftover 2, 3, 4, 5 has nth term n+1n + 1
Answer
nth term =2n2+n+1= 2n² + n + 1 (check: n=1n = 1 gives 2+1+1=42 + 1 + 1 = 4)
⚠️ Watch out
the coefficient of n2n² is half the second difference, not the second difference itself.
Calculate
?Higher. Find the 10th term of the quadratic sequence 3, 9, 19, 33, 51, ….
Mission check

?On the chessboard, square 1 has 1 grain and each square doubles the one before. How many grains are on square 64?

The rule is not linear: each square multiplies by 2, so square nn holds 2n−12ⁿ⁻¹ grains. Square 64 holds 2632⁶³, about 9.2 billion billion grains, far more than adding would ever give.

Mission 24

Two runners' distance–time graphs cross. What does the crossing mean?

Make a guess: Two runners' distance–time graphs cross. What does the crossing mean?

Algebra · real-life graphs

Distance–time graphs

  • The gradient of a distance–time graph is the speed: distance ÷ time.
  • Steeper means faster. A horizontal line means stopped.
  • Where two graphs cross, the two objects are at the same place at the same time. If the lines do not have the same gradient there, one is overtaking the other.
  • Use the units on the axes: metres per minute, km/h, m/s.
Worked example Algebra · real-life graphs

Reading two runners' graphs

Question
Runner A runs 2000 m in 10 minutes at a steady pace. Runner B covers 1200 m in the first 4 minutes. Find each speed for the first 4 minutes, in m/s, and say who is faster at the start.
  1. 1
    Gradient of B's first section: 41200​=3001200/4 = 300 m per minute
  2. 2
    Convert to m/s: 4×601200​=51200/(4 × 60) = 5 m/s
  3. 3
    Gradient of A's line: 10×602000​=3.332000/(10 × 60) = 3.33 m/s (3 s.f.)
  4. 4
    Compare: B's line is steeper at the start
Answer
B runs at 5 m/s and A at 3.33 m/s, so B is faster at the start.
⚠️ Watch out
change minutes to seconds before dividing, or the answer is in metres per minute.
Calculate
?Exam-style. A cyclist rides 15 km in 45 minutes, stops for 15 minutes, then rides 15 km back home in 30 minutes. Find the average speed for the whole journey.
km/h
Algebra · real-life graphs

Conversion graphs and rates

  • A conversion graph is a straight line through (0,0)(0, 0): the two quantities are in direct proportion.
  • The gradient is the rate: kilometres per mile, euros per pound.
  • A line that starts above (0,0)(0, 0) has a fixed charge. A plumber charging £40 call-out plus £30 per hour has intercept 40 and gradient 30 (£ per hour).
  • Read across from one axis to the line, then down (or across) to the other axis.
Calculate
?The conversion graph is a straight line through (0,0)(0, 0) and (50 miles, 80 km). Use it to convert 28 miles to kilometres.
km
Algebra · real-life graphs

Gradient of a curve (Higher)

  • On a curve the gradient changes. Draw a tangent: a straight line that just touches the curve at the point.
  • The gradient of the tangent is the instantaneous rate of change there, e.g. the speed at that moment on a distance–time graph.
  • Pick two points far apart on the tangent: gradient = change in yy ÷ change in xx.
Calculate
?Higher. A tangent is drawn to a distance–time curve at t=3t = 3 s. It passes through (1, 2) and (5, 14), with time in seconds and distance in metres. Estimate the speed at t=3t = 3 s.
m/s
Mission check

?Two runners start together. Their distance–time graphs cross at (8 minutes, 1600 m). Runner B's line is steeper at the start. What does the crossing mean?

The crossing means both runners are at the same place at the same time: A overtakes B at 8 minutes, 1600 m from the start. B was faster at the start, because B's line was steeper.

Mission 25

Cycle out at 10 km/h, back at 30 km/h. Is your average 20 km/h?
